cards.explanation: The answer is that no one can stand against us. Paul asks, "If God is for us, who can be against us?" (Romans 8:31). He isn't saying no one will ever oppose us. He's saying that with God for us, no one can win against us. Picture someone standing next to the biggest, calmest person in the room, knowing who's beside them whatever comes at them.

The answer is that God will freely give us all things. Paul says God did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, so "…how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?" (Romans 8:32). Notice the word freely, friends. There's no invoice stuck to the back of this one. If He gave the biggest gift, the rest is no stretch.

The answer is justifies. Paul says, "It is God who justifies." (Romans 8:33). The One with the final say is the One who declares us right with Him. So anyone lining up to bring a charge is talking to the wrong office.

The answer is False. Paul asks, "Who is there to condemn us?" and then points to Christ Jesus (Romans 8:34). He points to Jesus as the one who died, was raised and is at God's right hand. He is interceding for us, not condemning us. Whew, friends, what a difference one answer makes.

The answer is hard things people suffer. Trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword are all things people go through (Romans 8:35). Paul names the rough stuff on purpose, friends. None of it is on the list of things that can cut us off from the love of Christ.

The answer is False. Paul asks who shall separate us from the love of Christ, lists the hard things, and then says, "No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us." (Romans 8:37). That No is doing a lot of work, bakers. Hard things are real, but they can't pull us away from Him.

The answer is more than conquerors. Paul says, "No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us." (Romans 8:37). Notice it's through Him who loved us, friends, not through our own muscle. I'd lift my mustache in a victory wave if I could lift it any higher.

The answer is creation. Paul says, "…neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God…" (Romans 8:39). Anything else in all creation is a big net, bakers. He leaves no corner of it open for something to sneak through.

The answer is True. Paul ends with "…the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 8:39). After all that building up, friends, he lands on a person, not an idea. That love is found in Christ Jesus, and nothing in all creation can pull us away from it.
